source: A Night Off design doc p. 10 (Conversation), p. 26 (Dialogue: text with gibberish voices, captioned; drunk captions substitute the spoken line), p. 40 (conversation math). Lines are ours; the doc asks for about 40 per regular in the end (stage 7).

ask: What's the story with you, then?
joke: A squid walks into a bar. Eight arms, no tip.
I'd tell you a joke about the Nautilus, but it'd go over your head. Underneath it, actually.
My captain says I drink like a fish. Fish drink water. Checkmate.
Why did the crab never share? He was shellfish.
challenge: Bet you can't back that up.
drunk_agree: You're my best friend. Who are you?
drunk_joke: Why did the... the thing... HA. I forget. HA.
Knock knock. No wait, I'M the door.
drunk_challenge: Your face is a hull with barnacles on.
I could take you. I could take anyone. Hold my drink. Hold me.

Talker: Oh! Sit, sit. Have I told you about my knee?
Hustler: You've got the look of someone who's good at pool.
Gambler: Got any money? Asking for a friend.
Sailor: Nautilus, eh? Bet my lot drinks yours under the table.
Oddball: The gulls are talking tonight. Did you hear?
Have you ever counted the bubbles in a pint?

ask_ok: Most people don't ask. Here's the thing.
joke_ok: HA! Oh, that's terrible. Tell another.
That's the worst thing I've heard all week. I love it.
joke_fail: I've heard better from the goat.
challenge_ok: Ha! You've got some brass. I like that.
challenge_fail: Say that again. I dare you.
You want to take this outside?
listen: ...so I says to him, I says...
...and that was the year of the eels...
...which is why I don't trust lighthouses...
end_good: Here, let me tell you something nobody knows...

laugh.text: A laugh shared: +5 charisma for 5 minutes

items: a matchbook from the Brass Monkey
